questions.q: A missile is fired for maximum range with a initial velocity of $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, the range of the missile is
questions.solution: For maximum range of projectile $\theta$ will be $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ by the law of projectile motion $\therefore \quad R_{\max }=\frac{u^2}{g}$ Given, $\quad u=20 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ and $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\begin{aligned} & R_{\max }=\frac{(20)^2}{10}=\frac{400}{10} \\ & R_{\max }=40 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two boys are standing at the ends $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ of a ground where $\mathrm{AB}=a$. The boy at $\mathrm{B}$ starts running in a direction perpendicular to $\mathrm{AB}$ with velocity $v_1$. The boy at A starts running simultaneously with velocity $v$ and catches the other in time $t$, where $t$ is:
questions.solution:
If boy \(A\) catches boy \(B\) in time \(t\),
\(\begin{aligned}
& \$Rightarrow(\m$mathrm{vt})^2=\left(\mathrm{v}}_{1} $\mathrm{t}\r$right)^2+\mathrm{a}^2 \\
& \Rightarrow $\m$mathrm{t}^2=\frac{\mathrm{a}^2}{\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{v}_1^2}$\\
& \Rightarrow $\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{v}_1^2}}$
\end{aligned}\)

Each person now moves with a uniform speed $v$ in such a way that $K$ always moves directly towards $L$, L directly towards $M$, $M$ directly towards $N$, and $N$ directly towards $K$. options: The four persons will never meet
questions.solution:
The velocity of K throughout the motion towards the centre of the square is $v$ $cos45 °$ and the displacement covered by this velocity will be KO.

$∴ t = \dfrac{KO}{vcos45 °} = \dfrac{( \sqrt{2} \dfrac{d}{2} )}{\dfrac{v}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{d}{v}$

questions.solution: From question $\begin{aligned} & r=\frac{20}{\pi} m, v=80 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \therefore \theta=2 \text { revolutions }=2 \times 2 \pi=4 \pi \mathrm{rad} \\ & \therefore \omega^2=\omega_0{ }^2+2 \alpha \theta \\ & \therefore \omega^2=2 \alpha \theta \ldots(\mathrm{i}) \text { since } \omega_0=0 \\ & \text { Since } \alpha=\frac{a}{r} \text { and } \omega=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{r} \end{aligned}$ Putting these values in eq. (i) $\begin{aligned} & \frac{V^2}{r^2}= \frac{2 a \theta}{r} \\ & \Rightarrow a= \frac{V^2}{2 r \theta}=\frac{80 \times 80}{2 \times\left(\frac{20}{\pi}\right) \times 4 \pi} \\ &=40 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A projectile has a maximum range of $16 \mathrm{~km}$. At the highest point of its motion, it explodes into two equal masses. One mass drops vertically downwards. The horizontal distance covered by the other mass from the time of explosion is
questions.solution:
Maximum range,
$R_{\max }=\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}=\frac{u^2}{g}=16 \mathrm{~km}$
Range is maximum when $\theta=45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ Initial momentum at the highest point
$=m u \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{m u}{\sqrt{2}}$
After explosion, the projectile breaks into two equal masses. As one mass drops vertically downwards, hence its velocity and momentum is zero in the $x$-direction.
Hence, if $v$ be the velocity of second mass, then according to law of conservation of momentum,
$m u \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{m}{2} v \quad \therefore \quad v=2 u \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$
Horizontal distance covered from the time of explosion
$\begin{aligned} & =v \times \frac{T}{2}=v \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 u \sin 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}}{g} \\ & =2 u \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \times \frac{u \sin 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}}{g} \\ & =\frac{u^2}{g} \times \sin 90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{u^2}{g}=16 \mathrm{~km}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A man crosses a river in a boat. If he crosses the river in minimum time, he takes $10min$ with a drift $120m$. If he crosses the river taking the shortest path, he takes $12 . 5min$, find the width of the river.
questions.solution:
Let ${v}_{r}$ = velocity of river

${v}_{br}$ = velocity of river in still water and

$w$ = width of river

Given, ${t}_\min = 10min$

or $\dfrac{w}{v\text{br}} = 10$ ...(i)

Drift, in this case, will be,

$x = {v}_{r}t$

$∴120 = 10{v}_{r}$ ...(ii)





The shortest path is taken when vb is along $AB$. In this case,

${v}_{b} = \sqrt{{v}_{br}^{2} - {v}_r^{2}}$

Now, $12\text{.}5 = \dfrac{w}{v\text{b}} = \dfrac{w}{{v}_{br}^{2} - {v}_r^{2}}$ ...(iii)

Solving these three equations, we get

${v}_{br} = 20m\min^{- 1}$,

${v}_{r} = 12m\min^{- 1}$

and $w = 200m$

The magnitude \left|\mathbf{v}_0\right|$ will be (take, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution: Let object is at $B(x, y)$ after $t=\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~s}$ Then, $x=u_x \times t=v_0 \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \times \sqrt{2}=v_0$ and $y=u_y t-\frac{1}{2} a_y t^2=v_0 \left(\sin$45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\$right)\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{2}($10) $\times(\sqrt{2})^2 $=\left($v_0-10\right)$\mathrm{m}$Displacement $O B$ of particle is O $B=\sqrt{O A²+A B²}=\sqrt{v_0^2+\left(v_0-10\right)^2}$So, $\quad v_{\text {avg }}}}=\frac{O B}{t}=v_0$ or $O B=v_0 t\begin{array}{lrl} \Rightarrow$ \text{ and } $\sqrt{v_0^2+\left(v_0-10\right)^2}=$v_0 $\sqrt{2}$ \text{ and } \Rightarrow v_0^2+\left(v_0-10\right)^2=2 v_0^2 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } v_0-10= \pmv_0 \text{ and } 2 v_0=10 \Rightarrow v_0=5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \end{array}$

questions.solution:
$h = ltan ⁡ \beta - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{gsin ⁡ \alphal^{2}}{{v}_{0}^{2}\cos^{2} ⁡ \beta}$
${v}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{gsin ⁡ \alphal^{2}}{2\cos^{2} ⁡ \beta\left(ltan ⁡ \beta - h\right)}}$

questions.q: A particle is projected with velocity $2\sqrt{gh}$ so that it just clears two walls of equal height $h$, which are at a distance of $2h$ from each other. What is the time interval of passing between the two walls?
questions.solution:
Let $t$ be the time interval. Then,



$2h = \left({u}_{x}\right) ( t )$

or ${u}_{x} = \dfrac{2h}{t}$ ...(i)

Further, $h = {u}_{y}t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$

or $gt^{2} - 2{u}_{y}t + 2h = 0$

${t}_{1} = \dfrac{2{u}_{y} + \sqrt{4{u}_y^{2} - 8gh}}{2g}$

and ${t}_{2} = \dfrac{2{u}_{y} - \sqrt{4{u}_y^{2} - 8gh}}{2g}$

$t = {t}_{1} - {t}_{2} = \dfrac{4{u}_y^{2} - 8gh}{g}$

or ${u}_y^{2} = \dfrac{g^{2}\left(t\right)2}{4} + 2gh$ ...(ii)

Given, ${u}_x^{2} + {u}_y^{2} = \left(2\sqrt{gh}\right)2$

$\dfrac{4h^{2}}{\left(t\right)2} + \dfrac{g^{2}\left(t\right)2}{4} + 2gh = 4gh$

$\dfrac{g2}{4}\left(t\right)4 - 2gh\left(t\right)2 + 4h^{2} = 0$

\left(t\right)2 = \dfrac{2gh \pm \sqrt{4g^{2}h^{2} - 4g^{2}h^{2}}}{g^{2} / 2} = \dfrac{4h}{g}$

or $t = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}}

questions.q: A projectile is launched with an initial speed of $40ms^{- 1}$~at an angle $30 °$~above the ground. The projectile lands on a hillside $2 . 0s$~later. The net displacement from where the projectile was launched to where it hits the target is (Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Horizontal displacement covered,&

$x = \left(40cos30 °\right) \times 2 = 40\sqrt{3}m$

Vertical displacement covered,~

$y = \left(40sin30 °\right) \times 2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(- 10\right) \times {2}^{2} = 40 - 20 = 20m$

Hence, required displacement will be,~

$\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}} = 20\sqrt{13}m$

questions.q: If a stone is to hit at a point which is at a distance $d$ away and at a height $h$ above the point from where the stone starts, then what is the value of initial speed $u$, if the stone is launched at an angle $\theta ?$
questions.solution:
Using equation of motion for projectile in x and y-direction.

$\text{h} = \left(u \text\sin\theta\right)t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$

$d = \left(\text{u}\text\cos\theta\right)t$ or $t = \dfrac{d}{\text{u}\text\cos\theta}$

$⟹ h = u \text\sin\theta\text{.}\dfrac{d}{u \text\cos\theta} - \dfrac{1}{2}\text{g}\text{.}\dfrac{\text{d}2}{u^{2}\cos^{2}\theta}$

$⟹ \text{u} = \dfrac{d}{\text\cos\theta}\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2\left(\text{d}\text{t}an\theta - h\right)}}$
